newsitem.title: USA: Clinton leads Dole by 11 percent in Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton leads Dole by 11 percent in Reuters poll.

text.p: By Alan Elsner, U.S. Political Correspondent

U.S. President Bill Clinton leads Republican opponent Bob Dole by just over 11 percentage points while Republicans and Democrats are in a dead heat in congressional elections, according to a new Reuters poll released on Tuesday.

The poll, conducted by John Zogby Group International, was conducted from Saturday through Monday. It included 903 likely voters and carries a margin of error of plus or minus 3.3 percentage points. It begins a daily tracking poll that will carry through to Election Day, Nov 5.
Clinton leads Dole by 44.9 percent to 33.8 percent. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot trails with 5 percent and 14.4 percent said they were still undecided.
Pollster John Zogby said the poll showed the election was not over yet, as the candidates head into the first presidential debate on Sunday.
"Clinton has still not wrapped it up," he said.
When asked who they would vote for in their congressional district, voters divided almost equally, with 35.1 percent saying they would support Republicans and 35.6 percent backing Democrats.

That was encouraging news for Republicans, showing that Clinton may not have long enough coattails to carry his party back to control of Congress, two years after Republicans took control of both houses for the first time in 40 years.

The result showed the presidential race has changed very little since early August when a Reuters poll found Clinton leading Dole by 43.3 percent to 31.3 percent. But Dole has narrowed the race since the last national Reuters/Zogby poll on Sept 5, when the president led by 15 percentage points.
Dole trails by slightly less in this poll than in some other recent national surveys, but there was little real cheer for the Republican nominee.

He is still gaining only 68 percent of Republican voters, while Clinton is backed by 84 percent of Democrats. Clinton is also taking the support of more than a quarter of voters describing themselves as conservtive.
Clinton leads among every age group except those aged 50 to 64, where Dole enjoys a seven-point advantage.

Clinton's lead is more than 20 points on both the East and West Coast and he retains a narrow lead in the South. The race is virtually even in the important central states, including the Great Lakes states.

Unlike other polls, this survey found little difference between the voting intentions of men and women. Dole is running even with Clinton among whites but trails badly among black and Hispanic voters.
Some 49 percent of respondents said Clinton deserves re-election and 41 percent feel the country is on the right tracks, compared to 40 percent who think it is heading in the wrong direction.
Dole has spent the past two weeks attacking Clinton as a "tax-and-spend liberal". The poll found that 37.5 percent agreed with that assessment, but 50.1 percent disagreed.
If the election for president were held today, for whom would you vote, Clinton, Dole, or Perot?
